summary: Skagit County, WA: register lists an 83-ft 1941 tower, now gone; Willhite doubts it and documents a 1942 AWS cabin on private land; no tower confirmed.

facts.design: Register: 83-foot wooden tower with 7'x7' cab and cabin; Willhite doubts a tower stood here and documents an AWS 14x32 cabin
facts.status_note: Register and firelookout.com say the tower and cabin are gone; Forest Lookouts marks the site removed; a 2023 map found by new landowners confirms a fire lookout at this location, per Willhite

access.note: Private land per Willhite; new landowners since 2023; hikers report signs that claim a permit is needed. No current access rule found in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: Dirt road from the small town of Wickersham to a gate with parking; on the Pacific Northwest Trail per Willhite. Ask the landowners before going.

events.note: Register and firelookout.com: 83-ft wooden tower with 7x7 cab and cabin built in 1941. Willhite cites the Kresek inventory for the same date but doubts a tower stood on this site.
AWS Station Yoke 1-7 activated September 2, 1942 under the Bellingham Filter Center; AWS funds built a 14x32 cabin on private property (construction date not given)
Registered May 22, 2012 on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register; nominated by Ray Kresek
New landowners found a map confirming a fire lookout at this location (Willhite 2023 update); the area was recently pre-commercially thinned

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com describe an 83-foot wooden tower built in 1941. Willhite doubts the Kresek inventory behind that date and documents only an AWS cabin, but his 2023 update says a map confirms a fire lookout at this location. The story says the tower is not confirmed and reports both accounts.
The register gives 3,365 ft (1,026 m) and firelookout.com gives 3365 ft; Willhite gives about 2,400 ft. The story reports both figures.

Forest Lookouts gives 36N-4E-2 (section 2), and the Kresek inventory puts it on Anderson Mountain in section 2; Willhite's AWS station list places it in the NE quarter of the SE quarter of section 5. The story reports the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: The tower, its 1941 date and its 83-foot height rest on the register and firelookout.com, which both appear to draw on the Kresek inventory that Willhite questions. The AWS cabin (activated September 2, 1942, 14x32 feet, on private land) is documented in Forest Lookouts and Willhite's AWS page, and is the best-supported built feature. Willhite's 2023 update is the only source on the site's present condition and says a map confirms a fire lookout at this location, so the story does not treat the tower as disproved. The story does not give a removal date, since none appears in the sources. Access is recorded as permission because the land is private and hikers report permit signs; no owner or current rule was found. Brief's elevation 1025.7 m matches the register. Used 6 page reads (including the Wikipedia AWS definition and the Willhite AWS station list) and 1 WebSearch.
